method: Full pinned file read; Git blob verified. Original Program.run AST-extracted and executed with deterministic time, subprocess, cache-flush and statistics stubs; no real scanner process or system cache modification.
findings: Program.run catches CalledProcessError then computes averages using configured n_runs even when fewer samples exist. First-run failure yields all-zero averages; partial runs are biased downward. No explicit failure field prevents storing these as benchmark results.

Across sub-runs it keeps fastest elapsed time plus matching CPU/memory values, but independently overwrites duplicate/group counters with later successful parsing. Thus one stored row may combine timing from one attempt with counts from another.
Timing uses time.time rather than a monotonic clock. Programs run sequentially; each sub-run flushes caches then runs three iterations. This is not alternating paired comparison.

Global /tmp/.cpu_usage and /tmp/rmlint.json paths allow concurrent or stale-file interference. read_time_info returns scalar zero on OSError although caller unpacks two values; malformed file parsing exceptions are not caught. memory_usage is initialized -1 and never updated, even though row peak memory is separately recorded.

Command construction joins unquoted path strings and uses shell=True, so literal whitespace/metacharacter paths are not preserved as argument boundaries. Rdfind output option is concatenated with joined input paths without a separating space.

Install skips rebuild whenever a cached binary exists; early return when no install procedure exists occurs before finally restoring cwd. Rmlint246 references a build script absent from the pinned tree inventory.
No expected-content partition gate runs before timing. Defaults datasets None is iterated unconditionally in main, so invoking without -d can fail before useful work.

executed_control.scope: Original method under synthetic subprocess and clock dependencies; verifies accounting behavior, not measured performance.

limits: No production change, upstream benchmark execution or new performance result.
